quotes.quote: The Company respectfully disagrees with the jury’s findings and plans to vigorously contest the verdict and judgment through post-trial motions in the district court, and through an appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit if required.
however, in the absence of the receipt of additional financing, we will be required to curtail or cease operations and/or seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws.
The jury awarded Qorvo approximately $38.6 million in damages.
Qorvo may seek an award of attorneys’ fees.
The Company believes that its XBAW products incorporating previously disclosed design updates are not affected by this verdict.

While we cannot currently determine the ultimate liability pursuant to this verdict, if we are unable to reduce the verdict prior to the rendering of a final judgment by the court or to reach a reasonable settlement with Qorvo and depending on any equitable relief granted, we would be liable to pay substantial damages in excess of our liquid assets.

Any or all of the foregoing would materially harm our business, fundamentally change our business, and could result in our being required to take actions to discontinue operations or liquidate part or all of our operations and/or seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws.
The verdict and recovery of damages is subject to customary post-trial motions and potential appeals.
The jury awarded Qorvo approximately $38.6 million in damages.
As of March 31, 2024, we had approximately $15.2 million of cash and cash equivalents.
we believe there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Absent an increase in the shares of common stock authorized for issuance under our Certificate of Incorporation, we will be limited to non-equity financing structures in the event additional financing is required.
Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.

however, in the absence of the receipt of additional financing, we will be required to curtail or cease operations and/or seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws.
The jury awarded Qorvo approximately $38.6 million in damages.
Qorvo may seek an award of attorneys’ fees.
The Company believes that its XBAW products incorporating previously disclosed design updates are not affected by this verdict.

While we cannot currently determine the ultimate liability pursuant to this verdict, if we are unable to reduce the verdict prior to the rendering of a final judgment by the court or to reach a reasonable settlement with Qorvo and depending on any equitable relief granted, we would be liable to pay substantial damages in excess of our liquid assets.

Any or all of the foregoing would materially harm our business, fundamentally change our business, and could result in our being required to take actions to discontinue operations or liquidate part or all of our operations and/or seek protection under applicable bankruptcy laws.
The verdict and recovery of damages is subject to customary post-trial motions and potential appeals.
The jury awarded Qorvo approximately $38.6 million in damages.
As of March 31, 2024, we had approximately $15.2 million of cash and cash equivalents.
we believe there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
we effectively have 3.0 million available unissued and unreserved authorized shares to meet the needs of our business.

Absent an increase in the shares of common stock authorized for issuance under our Certificate of Incorporation, we will be limited to non-equity financing structures in the event additional financing is required.
Additionally, the terms of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 impose certain limitations on our ability to incur additional debt obligations.

the amounts outstanding under our $44.0 million principal amount of our 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 and a $4.0 million promissory note issued in connection with our acquisition of GDSI (including the potential we may experience one or more defaults or events of default under such instruments); and

the uncertainty that the approximately $38.6 million judgment awarded to Qorvo in the Qorvo Litigation has created regarding our financial condition and prospects and potential negative impact on our ability to raise additional capital.

we may be forced to undertake additional measures, which may include delaying or reducing our R&D plan and/or manufacturing and sales activities, materially curtailing or eliminating our operations, selling or disposing of our rights or assets, pursuing sale or other strategic transactions, or undergoing restructuring or insolvency proceedings.
